claims.content: The Customer wants to register a new free membership account on the JTVauctions.com website.
Customer
The JTVauctions.com site does not offer Guest Checkout; only registered users may use the auction site.
The customer registration process consists of two distinct pages: a first page for minimum required information and a second page for additional shipping and email preference information.
Neither registration page includes Endeca left navigation.
Both registration pages use the global header and/or footer.
The Privacy Policy page and Terms of Use page exist as Phase 1 must-have requirements and use the global site header and footer.

The customer must not have an existing account with the same email address; no two accounts may use the same email address, and the system will notify the registrant if the email address is already in use.

To prevent duplicate accounts, no new account may be created with the same combination of first name, last name, and street address as an existing account; the customer is informed if such a match is found.
For a new customer, the Consumer Protection negative file must be cross-referenced before the account can be successfully established.

The use case is triggered when a new customer clicks the 'Register Now' button/link — either the large 'Register Now' button in the New User registration section on the Sign-in page or the 'Register Now' link in the global footer — to create a new JTVauctions.com account.

The system starts the two-page registration process by displaying Registration Page 1 (the 'short process') with the global site header/footer, a welcome headline 'Welcome to JTVauctions.com! Create your free membership account here.', and subtext explaining that this is the minimum information needed to place bids.
The customer enters First Name, Last Name, Email Address (entered twice for verification), Password (8-12 characters, entered twice), and Member ID ('Handle') into the User Information Section.
The customer selects a default payment method via radio buttons: Credit Card, PayPal, or Amazon Payments.

If Credit Card is selected, the customer enters Credit Card Type, Credit Card #, Expiration Date, and Billing Address; if PayPal or Amazon Payments is selected, the system provides links to sign up or log in to those services (opening in a new browser tab).

The customer checks the checkbox to accept the JTVauctions.com Terms of Use Agreement, which is required to participate in auctions; the 'Finish Now' and 'I Want to Sign in Now' buttons remain grayed out until this checkbox is checked, and clicking a grayed-out completion button triggers a pop-up message requiring agreement.
The customer clicks 'Finish Now' to proceed to Registration Page 2 and complete additional shipping and email preference information.

The system displays Registration Page 2 ('Continuing Your Membership Creation'), pre-populating the My Information Section fields (First Name, Last Name, Email, Password, Member ID/Handle) from Page 1.
The customer enters a Phone Number in the My Information section.

The customer enters or confirms their Billing Address (Address 1, Address 2, Suite/Apt, City, State, Zip, Country) and Shipping Address; the 'Same as Billing Address' checkbox is available to duplicate the billing address into the shipping fields, or the customer may uncheck it and enter separate shipping details.
The customer selects a shipping preference via radio button in the My Shipping Preferences section: USPS Standard or Expedited (5-day, add $5.00).
The system displays a warning note that these shipping preferences apply only to credit card orders; PayPal/Amazon users choose shipping during their respective checkout processes.
The customer sets email notification preferences by checking boxes for 'outbid', 'winner', and 'shipping' transactional emails, and may access a link to change newsletter subscriptions.
The customer clicks the 'Save Changes' button to complete the registration process.

The system displays a pop-up message instructing the customer to add JTV's email address(es) to their safe senders list/address book and to enable cookies in their browser; the registration process includes instructions on adding JTV email addresses to the whitelist/safe senders list.

The system sends a registration confirmation email with a Thank You message, instructions to enable cookies, and instructions to add the appropriate email address(es) to the whitelist or Safe Senders list.

Diverges from Step 4: If the customer selects PayPal or Amazon Payments as the default payment method instead of Credit Card, the system does not present the credit-card/billing-address entry fields; instead, it provides links to sign up for or log in to those services, and those links open in a new browser tab.

Diverges from Step 5: If the customer clicks either the grayed-out 'Finish Now' button or the grayed-out 'I Want to Sign in Now' button before checking the Terms of Use checkbox, a pop-up message appears requiring the customer to read and agree to the Terms of Use before proceeding; the pop-up states: 'You must check this box to agree to our Terms of Use in order to participate in JTVauctions.com auctions.'

Diverges from Step 6: Instead of clicking 'Finish Now' to continue to Registration Page 2, the customer clicks 'I Want to Sign in Now' (also labelled 'Browse Now') to finish account creation and is taken to the sign-in page; if the customer was browsing before registering, they are returned to their last product details page, otherwise to the home page, and they may defer entering shipping information until a later time.

Diverges from Step 10: If the customer's default payment method is PayPal or Amazon Payments, the shipping preference selection on Registration Page 2 (USPS Standard or Expedited) does not apply; the customer is not required to select a shipping preference on this page, because shipping options are presented during the PayPal/Amazon checkout process instead. The system displays a warning note to this effect.

Diverges from Step 12: If the customer's default payment method is PayPal or Amazon Payments, the 'winner' email notification is mandatory and cannot be opted out of, regardless of any email preference settings selected on Registration Page 2.

Diverges from Main Flow Step 2 (User Information entry). Triggering condition: The registrant attempts to create a new account using an email address that already exists in the database. System response: The system prevents duplicate account creation, notifies the registrant that the email address is already in use, and asks whether they need to reset the password for the existing account; if the user confirms, the system sends an email with a temporary password to that email address. Exit: The registration attempt terminates without creating a new account; the customer is directed toward the password-reset/existing-account recovery path.

Diverges from Main Flow Step 5 (Terms of Use Agreement). Triggering condition: The customer clicks a grayed-out completion button ('Finish Now' or 'I Want to Sign in Now') before checking the Terms of Use Agreement checkbox. System response: The system displays a pop-up message requiring agreement: 'You must check this box to agree to our Terms of Use in order to participate in JTVauctions.com auctions.' Exit: The use case returns to Main Flow Step 5; the customer must check the Terms of Use checkbox before the completion button becomes active and the registration can proceed.

Diverges from Main Flow Step 9 (Billing/Shipping Address entry). Triggering condition: The system detects that the combination of first name, last name, and street address entered by the customer matches an existing account. System response: The system blocks creation of a new account, informs the customer that an account already exists, and offers to send sign-in information to the email address on file for that account. Exit: The use case terminates without creating a new account; the customer is redirected toward recovering the existing account rather than completing registration.

Diverges from Main Flow Step 13 (final registration submission/account establishment). Triggering condition: The Consumer Protection negative file cross-reference identifies a match for the new customer before the account is established. System response: The system prevents account creation and displays the exact error message: 'We are sorry, we are unable to create an auction account for you at this time. If you believe this message to be in error, please contact our Customer Service team at: 800-550-8393.' Exit: The use case terminates; no account is created.

A new JTVauctions.com customer account is successfully created and persisted in the database with a unique Member ID/Handle and a unique, verified email address (entered twice and checked for uniqueness). The account record is populated with all data entered during both registration pages — First Name, Last Name, Email Address, Member Handle, Phone number, Password (masked), Billing Address, Shipping Address, Shipping Preference (if credit card selected), default payment method, and email notification preferences — and this data is stored and displayed on the My Account page.

After successful full registration (via 'Finish Now' to Registration Page 2 and then 'Save Changes'), the system displays the My Account page (titled 'My Membership Account') as the final post-registration state. The page presents the registered customer's data in read-only form with EDIT buttons/links to the My Account Edit pages and a 'SAVE CHANGE' button for preferences; it uses the global site header/footer, does not include Endeca left navigation, and includes a link to the 'Returning Winners Payments' page.

The My Account page displays a personalized welcome message based on cookie or sign-in data (e.g., 'Welcome, Rick!' at the top right; 'Not Rick? Sign in here.'), confirming that the newly registered user is recognized/logged in immediately after registration.

Configuration choices made during registration are saved as the default system state for the new account: the selected shipping preference radio button is checked (e.g., 'Expedited (5-day, add $5.00)') and the default payment method is selected/displayed (e.g., Credit Card with card type, last four digits, and expiration date).

Shipping preferences set during registration (Standard or Expedited) apply only to credit card orders; PayPal and Amazon Payments users are given shipping options during their respective checkout processes instead.

For customers whose default payment method is PayPal or Amazon Payments, the system enforces a mandatory 'winner' email notification that cannot be opted out of, regardless of the email-preference checkbox settings selected on the registration page.

After successful registration, the system displays a pop-up message instructing the customer to add JTV's email address(es) to their safe senders list/address book (where specified, shop@jewelryTV.rsys1.com) and to enable cookies in their browser.

The system sends an automated transactional registration confirmation email after successful completion — whether the customer completes the full process via 'Finish Now' to Page 2/'Save Changes' or the short process via 'Browse Now' on Page 1. The email contains a Welcome/Thank You message using the customer's real name stating 'You are now registered with JTV Auctions!'.

The registration confirmation email also includes: instructions to enable cookies; instructions to add the appropriate JTV email address(es) to the whitelist/Safe Senders list/address book (including Shop@jewelrytv.rsys1.com for Responsys emails and [acnauction@jewelrytelevision.com or appropriate JTV email address] for JTV-sent transactional emails); an invitation to subscribe to the Auction Insider Newsletter with a link or form; and a prompt to add www.jtvauctions.com to Favorite Links in the browser.

The system includes instructions on how to add JTV email addresses to the user's whitelist/safe senders list in three locations: during the registration process, on the My Account page, and in the subsequent registration confirmation email.

If the customer used the 'Browse Now' option to finish account creation without completing Registration Page 2, the system redirects to the sign-in page; if they were previously browsing, they are returned to their last product details page, otherwise to the home page.

The system initializes the newly created customer account with empty Order History and Bid History sections (column headers present, no data rows), ready to receive future transaction and bidding records.
